title: How Your Eyes Turn Light Into Sight
post_title: How Your Eyes Turn Light Into Sight | QuantaTale
post_description: How the eye focuses light into signals for the brain and how common vision problems are, from the NIH and WHO. Sources: National Institutes of Health https://www.nei.nih.gov/eye-health-information/healthy-vision/how-eyes-work and World Health Organization https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/blindness-and-visual-impairment #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: How does light become the picture you see? Light enters through the cornea, the clear dome at the front, which bends it to help the eye focus. The coloured iris adjusts how much light the pupil admits. The lens and cornea together focus light onto the retina, where photoreceptor cells turn it into electrical signals. Those signals travel along the optic nerve to the brain, which converts them into the image you see. The World Health Organization reports that billions of people worldwide have impaired near or distance vision. For almost half of them, the impairment could have been prevented or has not yet been addressed. Uncorrected refractive error is a leading cause of impaired vision in every country, among children and adults alike. Glasses for refractive error and cataract surgery are among the most cost-effective health-care interventions there are.
